matt: Heads up — after flipping LL128 + proto algo on the 8xA100 cluster for small-batch inference we see a ~22% regression in tokens/sec and higher tail latency. KV-cache hit rate dropped from ~93% to ~76% on the same workload. attaching short profiler excerpt below.

anika: ugh. can you paste the exact NCCL env and runtime flags used? also topology (p2p links) pls.

matt: repro run command + env:
```
export NCCL_PROTO=proto
export NCCL_ALGO=tree
export NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=GROUP
export NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS=4
./serve_benchmark --gpus 8 --batch-size 1 --seq-len 512 --model path/to/model
```
Topology: 4x NVLink pairs (mesh-ish), PCIe fallback to hostbridge for some pairs.

raj: curious — did you change our kernel selector? LL128 sometimes requires different GEMM kernels for small batch sizes.

matt: kernel selector unchanged. only toggled NCCL proto + bumped channels from 2 -> 4. selector logs show we still pick the same CUDA kernels, but compute timelines show more stalls during all-reduce phases.

emily: can you paste a short perf trace snippet (compute vs comm timeline)? even a flamechart screenshot description helps.

matt: paste from perf:
```
[0.0s - 0.12s] kernel GEMM_A
[0.12s - 0.13s] allreduce start (channel 3)
[0.13s - 0.20s] waiting on allreduce (blocked)
[0.20s - 0.35s] KV cache refill kernel
[0.35s - 0.50s] kernel GEMM_B
```
Notice increased gaps between compute kernels where KV cache refill overlaps with allreduce leading to extra stalls.

sasha: possible hypothesis: LL128 + proto pushes more small-message collectives across channels causing inter-channel contention, and KV traffic (small-ish memcpy-ish ops) competes with NCCL for PCIe/NVLink.

anika: makes sense. try two quick experiments: 1) reduce NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS back to 2, 2) force NCCL_PROTO=ll128 but NCCL_ALGO=ring (or disable proto) to see algo interaction. also toggle our KV warmup to prefetch more into device cache before allreduce.

matt: ran the experiments:
- NCCL_MAX_NCHANNELS=2 -> perf recovered ~14% (still -8% vs baseline)
- NCCL_PROTO=ll128 + NCCL_ALGO=ring -> perf recovered ~18% (down only ~4%)
- aggressive KV prefetch (prime top-k entries before inference loop) -> recovered ~9% on top of channel=2 case

emily: interesting that ring + ll128 does better than proto+tree. maybe proto/tree is picking collectives that favor large-message throughput and hurt small-message latency.

raj: another angle: kernel selector warmup. if the selector switches kernels at runtime depending on sequence/beam shapes, that churn could align poorly with NCCL scheduling. do you have per-kernel warmup stats?

matt: we do. after long runs kernel selection becomes stable, but the regression appears quickly (within first 100 requests) — points to interaction with KV cache population and channel scheduling rather than pure kernel churn.

ci-bot: [perf-ci] New perf job 2129990000-rl-smallbatch reported: baseline 9800 tok/s, current 7640 tok/s (-22.0%). See /ci/artifacts/2129990000 for traces.

anika: next steps:
- Create a minimal reproducer that isolates KV memcpy vs NCCL traffic (separate streams)
- Try NCCL_P2P_LEVEL adjustments and NCCL_ALGO overrides to force ring vs tree
- Add an opt-in path in runtime to pre-warm KV cache before launching inter-GPU collectives
- Run microbenchmarks with different channel counts and measure per-channel bandwidth + latency

sasha: I'll add a quick allreduce micro-bench that simulates our small-message sizes and measures tail lat with multiple channels. can we try on a hetero link set too?

matt: thanks. i'll open a short issue with the numbers and attach traces + env dump. putting a tentative label perf/regression + nccl/channel-algo.

emily: if anyone wants to pair on the reproducer today i'm free after 4pm PST. :coffee:

matt: great — pairing welcome. i'll drop the reproducer and a small script that toggles env flags in the issue.
